purpose: Continue the Osiris temporal investigation by correcting the later conversational misreading of the Sirius light-time model and testing source-bound recurrence/interval candidates across Pyramid Texts, Abydos, Dendera/Khoiak, Plutarch, and Sothic records.

correction.correction_statement: 2035 is not an established Osiris-return date. The canonical repository already separated Sirius light travel from ritual prophecy. The erroneous 27.11.2035 return statement was a later conversational/post-hoc interpretation and is retracted without rewriting the historical artifact.

frozen_question: Does a source-independent temporal interval recur across the dated witness chain Unas/Pyramid Texts -> Abydos -> Dendera/Khoiak -> Sirius/Sopdet astronomical records strongly enough to justify an Osiris return interval?

source_chain.finding: The earliest pyramid containing Pyramid Texts is that of Unas. The specific JANUS stellar operators currently frozen for PT442/PT477 are later Old Kingdom witnesses used from Pepi I, not a license to attribute those exact passages to Unas.
source_chain.sothic_control: A 2025 high-precision chronology study states that no reliable Old Kingdom Sothic record is currently available; proposed Dynasty V Sothic readings remain speculative/debated.

source_chain.finding: Abydos stelae and museum synthesis attest an annual Osiris death/resurrection festival. Mentuwoser's stela is dated to regnal year 17 of Senusret I. Ikhernofret/Sisatet evidence places a royal Osiris commission/festival context in regnal year 19 of Senusret III.

Plutarch reports the trapping/killing deed on day 17 of Athyr, in the 28th year of Osiris's reign or, in another version, life. He later describes a rite on the 19th day when a joyful cry announces that Osiris is found.
source_chain.boundary: LATE_GREEK_LITERARY_RITUAL_TRADITION; 17 ATHYR DATES THE INITIAL DEED, NOT THE LATER DISMEMBERMENT/PHALLUS LOSS.

source_chain.finding: The source comparison preserved by UCL gives a ritual recovery sequence in month IV Akhet/Khoiak, including head on day 19, phallus in variant entries on day 25 or 28, and Djed raising on day 30. The rites are described as recurring yearly.

Sopdet/Sirius heliacal rising is an annual astronomical event used as a calendrical anchor. The civil calendar and the heliacal rising phase-align only about once per 1460 Egyptian civil years because the 365-day civil calendar drifts relative to the solar year.

One of the earliest Sothic records is the Illahun Papyrus assigned to regnal year 7 of Senusret III. A 2025 PLOS ONE chronology study supports the High chronological placement of the Middle Kingdom and notes historical disagreement over absolute placement of the Sothic observation.
source_chain.cross_control: Ikhernofret/Sisatet Osiris activity is associated with regnal year 19 of the same king, producing a 12-regnal-year separation between these two documentary horizons, but no ancient source links that separation to an Osiris death/return interval.

interval_matrix.meaning: Plutarchian initial death/trapping date to ritual 'Osiris found' day

interval_matrix.calculation: (30-17) + 30 = 43 because Hathor/Athyr is month III Akhet and Khoiak is month IV Akhet, each 30 days
interval_matrix.meaning: Cross-source arithmetic span from Plutarch's 17 Athyr to the Khoiak Djed-raising endpoint
Abydos death/resurrection festival, yearly Khoiak rites, and annual Sopdet heliacal rising all recur on yearly cadences
Approximate recurrence of civil New Year and Sirius heliacal rising phase alignment
Documentary separation between Illahun Sothic record and Ikhernofret/Sisatet Osiris commission/festival horizon under Senusret III

observations: Plutarch: death in 28th year of reign/life.
Plutarch explicitly interprets 28 as the number of the moon's illuminations / lunar cycle.
Papyrus Jumilhac comparison: one variant places finding the phallus/arm on Khoiak day 28.
motif_28.independence: LOW_TO_MODERATE; sources participate in overlapping Osirian/lunar ritual traditions and are separated in date but not independent cultural experiments.
motif_28.interval_status: NOT_AN_INTERVAL; DO NOT TURN 28 INTO YEARS-TO-RETURN.

observations: Plutarch connects Osiris dismemberment into fourteen parts with the waning half of the lunar cycle.
Plutarchian ritual tradition: on the 19th day a joyful cry announces that Osiris is found.
Papyrus Jumilhac/Khoiak recovery table: on day 19 the head of Osiris is found.
Dendera Khoiak day-19 control: the Osiris figure is removed from the Sokar mould and enters the drying/wrapping ritual sequence.
motif_19_recovery.boundary: THE PLUTARCHIAN DAY 19 IS IN THE ATHYR/HATHOR MOURNING CONTEXT; THE JUMILHAC/DENDERA DAY 19 IS KHOIAK. SAME DAY NUMBER + RECOVERY SEMANTICS DOES NOT ESTABLISH SAME CALENDAR EVENT.
motif_19_recovery.independence: LOW; these witnesses may inherit overlapping late Osirian ritual traditions. A textual-dependence test is required before counting this as independent recurrence.

observations: Plutarch: 17 Athyr is the trapping/killing day.
Dendera/Khoiak day 17 concerns ritual preparation/watering rather than the killing of Osiris.

tests: Do not transfer the date of an inscription to the date of a mythic event.
Require an explicit ancient synchronizer before phase-locking Sirius to a Khoiak restoration day.
Treat repeated numbers as candidates only; reject dimension changes such as years -> days unless an ancient source makes the conversion.
Use dated witnesses as provenance anchors, not prophecy anchors.
Count annual recurrence separately from exact phase synchronization.
topa_gate.best_current_answer: The surviving evidence supports a yearly Osirian ritual return/revival cadence and short intra-cycle markers, but does not support a unique multi-year date for a future physical return of Osiris.
